items.index: RL OG Rise of Middle Class
items.title: The enormous rise of the middle class in certain developing countries is one of the greatest economic successes of the late 20th and early 21st centuries. This is excellent for the economies of those countries because the middle classes usually earn more than they need to live on, and thus they can save money. It's important that economists understand how these processes work, and thus they need to understand the savings habits of the new middle class. Our research, therefore, aimed to investigate patterns of savings and reasons for savings decisions. The country we chose to focus on was India. We found that, not surprisingly, it was the richer people, especially business owners, who tended to save more. As for the reasons for saving, the number one reason was to provide an income after retirement. Having an income after becoming too old to work was important for savers who wanted to be able to enjoy their older years. And the second most important reason was for family purposes, such as the education and weddings of their children.

items.index: RL OG Health and Food Guidance
items.title: I think there are a lot of confusing messages about health and food out there that don't really help the cause. Look at the most recent debate, fat versus sugar, two things that we know, scientifically, are of concern. And I think a big problem is that in the field of nutrition science, we look at individual nutrients like fat, carbohydrates, protein, etc, to figure out the metabolic consequences of food. And so when we're putting out public guidance about what we should be eating, we talk in terms of nutrients instead of converting those nutrients into foods like fish, fruit, cookies, and so on. But I think talking about foods rather than nutrients is an important step we need to take. At the same time, we don't have to say to people, you can eat this or you can't eat that. But we should help give people a wider view of the relative proportions of various food groups and dietary patterns on the whole.

items.title: The elephant is the largest living land mammal. During evolution, its skeleton has greatly altered from the usual mammal, designed for two main reasons. One is to cope with the great weight of huge grinding cheek teeth and elongated tusk, making the skull particularly massive. The other is to support the enormous bulk of such a huge body.

items.title: As you probably know, coffee is the second largest commodity by traded value in the world, after oil. You probably also know that it's grown in Brazil, but you may not realize that it's not native to that country. It originated in East Africa. So if it came from there, how did it cross the Pacific? Well, the Dutch took coffee to a number of different places around the world, including, including South America, where it thrived. Nowadays, all the coffee cultivated in Brazil comes from that one seedling, which was of a variety called robusto. Now, because it all comes from the one plant, genetically, robusto isn't particularly varied, which unfortunately means its resistance to disease is, well, rather on the low side. And, well, this is exactly what has happened recently. A pathogen called coffee rust is ravaging coffee crops across South America. So what it looks like is that the price of coffee is, well, going to skyrocket on the wholesale markets unless production is increased dramatically in a short space of time in other countries, such as, you know, Vietnam, which seems rather unlikely. So, in short, there's a good chance that your morning coffee is going to become, well, quite pricey, and pretty soon at that.
